summary: CRT-style FILE stream buffer teardown (MSVC __freebuf). Loads the stream flags word from this+0xC; when the flags have active I/O bits ((flags & 0x83) != 0) AND the buffer-ownership bit ((flags & 8) != 0), it frees the owned buffer pointer at this+0x8 via sub_58AA6F, clears the buffer-ownership flag bits by ANDing the flags word with 0xFBF7, zeroes the buffer base/count/allocation fields at this+0x0, this+0x4 and this+0x8, and returns 0. When the ownership guard fails, the original flags word is returned unchanged.

local_names.a1: FILE-style descriptor (a1[0]=read pointer, a1[1]=count, a1[2]=buffer pointer, a1[3]=flags)
local_names.result: stream flags word loaded from a1[3]

operations.description: Load the stream flags word from this+0xC. The deallocation branch runs only when the flags have I/O bits set ((flags & 0x83) != 0) and the buffer-ownership bit set ((flags & 8) != 0); otherwise the function returns the flags unchanged.
Free the owned buffer pointer at this+0x8 by calling sub_58AA6F, the OS-version-dispatched memory deallocation.
Clear the buffer-ownership flag bits: store (flags & 0xFBF7) back into the flags word at this+0xC as a 16-bit store.
result = 0 so the success path returns zero.
Zero the buffer start pointer at this+0x0 after freeing.
Zero the buffer count/position field at this+0x4 after freeing.
Zero the allocation pointer at this+0x8 after freeing.

Return the loaded flags word when the ownership guard fails, or 0 after a successful deallocation. Invoked by MSVCCRTFileClose (0x00587D33) and sub_59BB00 (0x0059BB00) as stream close/teardown; the ABI lead identifies this as MSVC_CRT___freebuf.

unresolved: The exact owning object (CRT FILE vs a custom stream object) is not evidenced in this packet; the struct layout matches the descriptor layout seen in neighboring stream functions.
Whether sub_58AA6F is the true CRT free or a shim is not evidenced here.
